response.hook: Some moons in our solar system are so big they would pass for planets.
response.intro: These are the ten largest moons, ranked by mean diameter.

segments.name: Oberon
segments.narration: Number ten: Oberon, the outermost of Uranus's major moons, at 1,523 kilometres wide. A frozen, cratered world we have seen up close only once.
segments.image_prompt: cinematic view of Oberon in space, no text

segments.name: Rhea
segments.narration: Number nine: Rhea. Saturn's second-largest moon edges past Oberon by just four kilometres, at 1,527.
segments.image_prompt: cinematic view of Rhea in space, no text

segments.name: Titania
segments.narration: Number eight: Titania, the biggest moon of Uranus, spanning 1,578 kilometres of ice and rock.
segments.image_prompt: cinematic view of Titania in space, no text

segments.name: Triton
segments.narration: Number seven: Triton. Neptune's giant measures 2,707 kilometres, and it is the only large moon that orbits backwards.
segments.image_prompt: cinematic view of Triton in space, no text

segments.name: Europa
segments.narration: Number six: Europa, the icy world scientists hope may hide an ocean, 3,122 kilometres across.
segments.image_prompt: cinematic view of Europa in space, no text

segments.name: The Moon
segments.narration: Number five is closer to home. Our own Moon, 3,475 kilometres wide, lighting every night sky on Earth.
segments.image_prompt: cinematic view of The Moon in space, no text

segments.name: Io
segments.narration: Number four: Io, the most volcanic place we know, at 3,643 kilometres.
segments.image_prompt: cinematic view of Io in space, no text

segments.name: Callisto
segments.narration: Number three: Callisto, battered and ancient, stretching 4,821 kilometres.
segments.image_prompt: cinematic view of Callisto in space, no text

segments.name: Titan
segments.narration: Number two: Titan, Saturn's hazy giant, at 5,150 kilometres. For a moment, it looks unbeatable.
segments.image_prompt: cinematic view of Titan in space, no text

segments.name: Ganymede
segments.narration: And number one: Ganymede. At 5,268 kilometres, Jupiter's king of moons is the largest in the entire solar system.
